editorial: You thought the Warrens' work had run its course, but The Conjuring: Last Rites throws them into a chilling final case that feels like a creeping dread on a slow canvas. The film’s unique blend of grounded investigative dialogue and perfectly orchestrated supernatural dread keeps your pulse racing during every unmade breath. A standout element is the unsettling, almost silent, presence of a shapeless entity that reminds you that some horrors are felt more than seen. Yet the pacing hiccups in the midway segment dilute the buildup, slightly breaking the tension that the rest of the film so masterfully builds. You’ll find yourself drawn in by the weighty atmosphere and uneasy curiosity that lingers long after the credits roll.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy non-linear storytelling.
